title: Well-posedness of pi: prove sum_mu F*_mu(q=1,t)=P*_lambda and positivity F*_mu(q=1,t)>=0 (so pi is a probability measure)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (L0).** Before any chain is constructed one must prove that
$$\pi(\mu)=\frac{F^*_\mu(x;q=1,t)}{P^*_\lambda(x;q=1,t)},\qquad \mu\in S_n(\lambda),$$
is an honest probability distribution. This requires two facts that are currently presupposed:

1. **Normalization (sum identity):** $\sum_{\mu\in S_n(\lambda)}F^*_\mu(x;q=1,t)=P^*_\lambda(x;q=1,t)$, so that $\sum_\mu\pi(\mu)=1$. This is the $q=1$ specialization of the BDW25a master/multiline-queue expansion $P^*_\lambda=\sum_\mu F^*_\mu$ and must be stated with matching index sets and conventions (cf. the open conventions gap q3-8).
2. **Nonnegativity:** $F^*_\mu(x;q=1,t)\ge 0$ and $P^*_\lambda(x;q=1,t)>0$ on an explicit parameter range (e.g. $0<t<1$, $0<x_1<\dots<x_n$). ASEP polynomials can carry signs before specialization, so positivity at $q=1$ is **not** automatic and needs a written factorization argument.

**Why the hypotheses matter.** The *restricted* condition (unique part $0$, no part $1$) should be used precisely to guarantee the denominator $P^*_\lambda(q=1,t)$ does not vanish (no collision of spectral/interpolation points) and that $S_n(\lambda)$ is the correct nondegenerate state space.

This is distinct from q3-5 (row-stochasticity of $P$) — it concerns the *target measure* $\pi$ itself.
